To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the decisions a person can take on an approval request:
requires_comment states which decisions always need a comment, whatever the
kind: a refusal and a reversal do, because the person who asked reads them. A
kind can ask for more, through its comment_on_approve flag.
Decision types are managed by the system tenant.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A request is decided by many decisions, not one: a kind may need two approvers,
and a hold, a return to waiting, a withdrawal, a refusal and a reversal are each
a decision of their own. Each is a row here, and a decision is never edited.
Two rules of the record are rules of the schema. The person who asked cannot
decide their own request, and a withdrawal is the one decision only they take:
a hand-written trigger in inbox_approval_decision_rules_create.sql checks
both. One person approves a request at most once: the unique index below
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the kinds of approval request. Examples:
A kind is the small declaration the generic record reads: the permission a
decider needs, whether the kind uses the held state, whether an approval
needs a comment, how long an unanswered request waits, and how many approvals,
each by a different person, close a request as approved. The component that
owns the kind owns its detail table and the operation that applies an approval.
Kinds are managed by the system tenant.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the parts of an approval: the functions whose approval
A part is what makes a request need several different people. Each part names the
permission a person needs to answer for it, and its answer_order: a part with a
lower order must approve before a part with a higher one can be answered, and parts
with the same order are answered in parallel. A request's parts are the distinct
parts of its changes, and the request is approved only when every one of them has
an approval. A refusal from a part that can be answered ends the request.
Parts are managed by the system tenant. A tenant without a function grants the
part's permission to whichever role does that work, so the part is decided by a
permission and not by a job title.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the approval policy: for an act on an entity, optionally
narrowed to one field, the part that must approve it. A row says that putting or
deleting an entity_type, or changing one of its fields, needs the named part. An
act with no row is written directly.
The policy is data, so who decides is a data change. The rows are the tables in
the book controls note: the description of a book needs no part, the cost center
needs finance, a move needs operations. One act may have several rows, one for each
part that must approve, and the request's parts are the distinct parts of its rows.
The system tenant holds the policy rows, so a tenant cannot loosen its own
controls. A tenant's own rows, which may add a part to an act and never remove one,
come with the policy read in a later task.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A request needs the approval of one or more parts, and a part may be needed by
many requests. Each row names one part a request needs, and is written when the
request is raised. A decision carries the part it answers, so a request is
approved when every part named here has an approval, in the order the parts give.
A request with no rows here is a request of a kind that names one decider
permission and a count, as the role request is, and it is decided as before.

Reference data table of the states of an approval request: 'waiting', 'held',
A final state has no exit but the ones the lifecycle names: approved can be
reversed with a comment, and refused, withdrawn and expired cannot be left
at all. The queue reads is_final to tell open requests from closed ones.
States are managed by the system tenant.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The header every kind of approval request shares: what is asked, who asked,
when and why, where the request is, and when it closes unanswered. What the
request is about lives in the kind's own detail table, owned by the component
that owns the kind and keyed by this request's id.
state_code is the state the request's decisions have reached. The decisions
The record is bitemporal, so every change of state is a version and the history
is the audit trail an auditor reads.

The outcomes of one attempt to reach a person through one channel: 'pending',
The set is closed, and the C++ enum domain::delivery_outcome holds the same
values. A code with no enum value cannot be read back, so the table is
immutable: it is seeded once and never changes at run time. Because it is
immutable, a delivery references it with a database foreign key rather than a
trigger check. The table has no tenant: the set is the same for every tenant.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The values a notification's message names, one row each: the role, the tenant,
the step. The screen renders the kind's message with them in the reader's
language, so a notification stores no finished sentence and no document.
A row is identified by the notification and the argument's name.

Reference data table of the ways a person is reached: 'in_app' and 'mail'. A
channel is a delivery of the same notification, not a different message.
Channels are managed by the system tenant.

One attempt to reach one recipient through one channel, and its outcome. A
recipient has many: a failed mail is retried, and each attempt is a row of its
own, so "were they told?" has an answer. A failed delivery never fails the
outcome is pending, delivered or failed, the C++ enum
domain::delivery_outcome. failure_reason says why a failed attempt failed,

Reference data table of the kinds of notification. Examples:
A notification carries a kind and its values, not a finished sentence. The kind
names the message key the screen renders in the reader's language. A component
adds a kind with a seed row and needs no change to the subsystem.
mail_optional says whether a person may turn the mail copy of this kind off.
A password recovery is a kind a person cannot turn off. The in-application copy
Kinds are managed by the system tenant.

Whether a person is reached through one channel for one kind. The key is the
account, the kind and the channel together, so a person holds one row for each
pair they have chosen; no row means the kind's default.
The in-application copy is always kept, and a kind that is not
mail_optional ignores a choice to turn its mail off. The service applies both

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Each person a notification reaches has their own row, kept until they read or
clear it, and a person reads only their own. read_at and cleared_at are the
person's read state: null until they read or clear it. The unread count on
every screen counts a person's rows with no read_at.
A row is identified by the notification and the account.

One thing that happened: its kind, who raised it and when, and where it is dealt
with. The values its message names are rows of
, and the people it reaches are rows of
, each with their own read state.
Every notification links to where it is dealt with: link_route names the
screen, and link_id names the thing on it, when there is one. A notification
never asks a person to act inside it, and it carries no password, token or
trade economics, because mail leaves the system.
When a notification is raised to every holder of a permission, the permission
is resolved into recipient rows at that moment, and audience_permission_code
